_about: Theodore Roosevelt's tours, trips and expeditions. Each has an original short line and summary written by the Library. Start and end dates are anchored to day entries in the TRA Chronological Record (cited in 'anchor'): the day he set out and the day he reached home or the record's last travel day. 'verified': false means an editor has not yet confirmed the boundary against a second source.

tours.title: The Family Grand Tour of Europe
tours.short: Ten-year-old Teedie's first trip abroad, kept in his own travel diary.
tours.summary: The whole family sails on the Scotia for a year in Europe. Teedie fights asthma along the way, walks in the woods of the Black Forest near Baden, writes to Edith Carow, gets homesick, and in Rome kisses the hand of Pope Pius IX. His sister Corinne later recalled that he had just whispered to the other American children that no real American believed in popes.
tours.anchor: 1869-05-12 sails on the Scotia; 1870-05-25 home to New York

tours.title: Egypt, the Holy Land and Dresden
tours.short: A year on the Nile, in the Holy Land and in Dresden, where a boy who already collected birds did his first serious collecting.
tours.summary: The Roosevelts sail again, this time for Egypt. On Christmas Day on the Nile his father gives him a double-barreled shotgun, and he shoots and skins birds all the way upriver. The family calls on Ralph Waldo Emerson, whose boat is moored near theirs. The trip runs on through the Holy Land and ends with the children spending the summer with German families in Dresden before the family comes home to a new house on 57th Street.
tours.anchor: 1872-10-16 sails on the Russia; 1873-11-05 home to 57th Street

tours.title: Prairie Hunt with Elliott
tours.short: Weeks of prairie shooting with his brother, from Illinois to the Red River country.
tours.summary: Newly engaged to Alice Lee and missing her every day, Roosevelt heads west with Elliott. The brothers shoot prairie chickens on an Illinois farm, spend a week hunting in Iowa, and finish near Fargo and Moorhead in the Red River valley. His sister Corinne later wrote that he always thought Elliott the better hunter of the two. Then it is home to Alice.
tours.anchor: 1880-08-16 leaves for Chicago with Elliott; 1880-09-29 back in New York

tours.title: Honeymoon in Europe with Alice
tours.short: A honeymoon abroad that took him to the top of the Matterhorn.
tours.summary: Married the October before, Roosevelt and Alice sail on the Celtic for nearly five months abroad. They tour Ireland, England and the Continent, and in the Alps he climbs the Jungfrau and the Matterhorn. News that President Garfield has been shot reaches him in the mountains; Garfield dies in September as the couple are about to sail for home.
tours.anchor: 1881-05-12 sails on the Celtic; 1881-10-02 home to New York

tours.title: First Buffalo Hunt in Dakota
tours.short: The month that brought him to the Badlands and made him a rancher.
tours.summary: Roosevelt steps off the train at Little Missouri at about three in the morning, hires Joe Ferris as his guide, and spends more than a week soaked, thrown and lost in pursuit of a buffalo before he finally gets one. Before the trip is out he goes into cattle with Sylvane Ferris and Bill Merrifield at the Chimney Butte ranch, known by its brand as the Maltese Cross. The Badlands chapter of his life begins here.
tours.anchor: 1883-09-03 leaves New York; 1883-10-02 last leg home

tours.title: A London Wedding and a Winter in Europe
tours.short: Across the Atlantic to marry Edith Carow, and a winter abroad as newlyweds.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sails with his sister Bamie, makes a lifelong friend of Cecil Spring Rice on board, and marries Edith at St. George's, Hanover Square, in London on a foggy December 2. The newlyweds spend the winter in Italy and France and come home in March to three-year-old Alice.
tours.anchor: 1886-11-06 sails for England; 1887-03-28 home in New York

tours.title: Hunting the Kootenai Country
tours.short: A hard hunt in the Selkirk Mountains of British Columbia.
tours.summary: From the Badlands Roosevelt travels by way of Idaho to Kootenai Lake in British Columbia and hunts the Selkirk Mountains with guide John Willis. After a week without luck the party rests and sets out again, and by his own account he comes out with a black bear and a caribou.
tours.anchor: 1888-08-26 bound for Idaho; 1888-10-04 eastbound for home

tours.title: The Rough Riders: San Antonio, Tampa and Santiago
tours.short: From training camp in San Antonio to the charge up Kettle Hill and home by way of Montauk.
tours.summary: Days after leaving the Navy Department, Lieutenant Colonel Roosevelt heads to San Antonio to help train the 1st U.S. Volunteer Cavalry. The regiment moves to Tampa, scrambles aboard the transport Yucatan at Port Tampa so it will not be left behind, and lands in Cuba in late June. It comes under fire at Las Guasimas, charges up Kettle Hill and the San Juan Heights on July 1, and holds the trenches outside Santiago until the city surrenders. Worn down by fever, the men sail for Montauk in August, where they give their colonel a Remington bronze before they are mustered out.
tours.anchor: 1898-05-12 leaves Washington for San Antonio; 1898-09-15 mustered out at Montauk, home to Sagamore Hill

tours.title: The Roosevelt Special
tours.short: The whistle-stop train that carried the Rough Rider to the governor's office.
tours.summary: Weeks out of uniform, Roosevelt crosses New York State on a campaign train with Rough Riders and reporters aboard. He takes on Richard Croker and the Tammany machine in town after town, turns 40 on the campaign trail, and is elected governor the day after his last swing through western New York.
tours.anchor: 1898-10-17 whistle-stopping up the Hudson; 1898-11-07 last swing through western New York

tours.title: West to the First Rough Rider Reunion
tours.short: Governor Roosevelt goes to Las Vegas, New Mexico, for the regiment's first reunion.
tours.summary: Governor Roosevelt travels west to rejoin his Rough Riders for their first reunion. On the way home he speaks in Illinois and Milwaukee, then tells reporters he is not a candidate for President in 1900.
tours.anchor: 1899-06-19 leaves for the West; 1899-06-29 back in Albany

tours.title: The 1900 Campaign Train
tours.short: Two months on the stump as McKinley's running mate, across the Midwest and the West.
tours.summary: As the Republican candidate for Vice President, Roosevelt carries the campaign west on a long rail tour: Labor Day in Chicago, about ten speeches in a day in Michigan, a brief stop in Medora, and a rough reception at Victor in Colorado's Cripple Creek mining district. Back east, he speaks to a huge Madison Square Garden rally on October 26, and on a rainy November 3, three days before the election, reviews a vast parade in Manhattan.
tours.anchor: 1900-09-02 bound for Chicago; 1900-11-03 reviews a parade in Manhattan

tours.title: Cougar Hunt in Colorado
tours.short: The Vice President-elect's winter hunt for mountain lions in Colorado.
tours.summary: Before taking office, Roosevelt rides out of Meeker with hunter John Goff and his hounds for five weeks of cougar and bobcat hunting in midwinter cold and snow. Several of the big cats he finishes with a knife while the dogs hold them. The biggest weighs 227 pounds.
tours.anchor: 1901-01-07 leaves to hunt cougar; 1901-02-23 home to Sagamore Hill

tours.title: New England Tour
tours.short: A swing through all six New England states that ended in a trolley crash.
tours.summary: President Roosevelt speaks across New England on regulating the trusts, from Connecticut to Maine and on through New Hampshire and Vermont. In Pittsfield, Massachusetts, a streetcar slams into his carriage. Secret Service agent William Craig is killed, and Roosevelt is thrown out, bruised and cut; a shin injury later becomes infected and needs surgery.
tours.anchor: 1902-08-22 Hartford; 1902-09-03 trolley crash at Pittsfield

tours.title: Wheeling, Chattanooga and North Carolina
tours.short: A short trip south only days after the Pittsfield crash.
tours.summary: Still bruised, Roosevelt speaks on the trusts at Wheeling, reviews cavalry at Chickamauga Park and tours the battlefields around Chattanooga by carriage, addresses the locomotive firemen's convention, and speaks in Asheville and Greensboro on the way home.
tours.anchor: 1902-09-05 leaves for Chattanooga; 1902-09-10 back to Oyster Bay

tours.title: Midwestern Tour, Cut Short
tours.short: A tour of the Midwest cut short by surgery in Indianapolis.
tours.summary: Roosevelt heads west with the coal strike unresolved, speaking in Cincinnati and Detroit. In Indianapolis doctors find that the leg hurt at Pittsfield needs surgery. The tour is called off; back in Washington he is lifted into a wheelchair at the station and driven to the temporary White House on Jackson Place to rest.
tours.anchor: 1902-09-19 starts west; 1902-09-23 surgery in Indianapolis; 1902-09-24 resting in Washington

tours.title: The Mississippi Bear Hunt
tours.short: The hunt that gave the teddy bear its name.
tours.summary: Roosevelt goes after bear in the canebrakes near Smedes, Mississippi. The newspapers carry the story that he would not shoot a bear that had been run down and tied for him, and Clifford Berryman's cartoon Drawing the Line in Mississippi makes the story widely popular.
tours.anchor: 1902-11-11 southbound by special train; 1902-11-21 back in Washington

tours.title: The Great Western Tour
tours.short: Nine weeks crossing the West by train.
tours.summary: Roosevelt leaves Washington on a nine-week tour of the West. He stops in the Badlands to see old friends, spends about two weeks in Yellowstone with John Burroughs, dedicates the St. Louis World's Fair, visits the Grand Canyon, and camps with John Muir in Yosemite, one night under the sequoias and another in the snow on the valley's rim. He rides some 62 miles on horseback from Laramie to Cheyenne before heading home.
tours.anchor: 1903-04-01 tour begins; 1903-06-05 home

tours.title: Hunting the Southwest
tours.short: A Rough Rider reunion in Texas, a coyote hunt in Oklahoma and a bear hunt in Colorado.
tours.summary: Early in his second term, Roosevelt addresses the Texas Legislature, speaks in front of the Alamo in San Antonio and spends an afternoon with his Rough Riders at their reunion, then gallops after coyotes with greyhounds in Oklahoma Territory alongside Jack Abernathy. He finishes with weeks of bear hunting in the Colorado mountains, breaking camp about a week earlier than planned.
tours.anchor: 1905-04-03 leaves Washington; 1905-05-11 home by midnight

tours.title: The Southern Tour
tours.short: Through the South to his mother's girlhood home, and back by sea.
tours.summary: With Edith along as far as Atlanta, Roosevelt speaks his way through the South from Richmond to New Orleans. He visits Bulloch Hall in Roswell, where his mother grew up, speaks at Tuskegee, and denounces lynching in Little Rock. From New Orleans he goes down the Mississippi and boards the armored cruiser West Virginia in the Gulf for the voyage home.
tours.anchor: 1905-10-18 leaves Washington; 1905-10-31 back at the White House

tours.title: Panama and Puerto Rico
tours.short: The first trip abroad by a sitting President: to see the canal being dug.
tours.summary: Roosevelt and Edith leave Washington on the Mayflower and board the battleship Louisiana to see the Panama Canal works for themselves. In steady rain he travels the line of the canal on the Panama Railroad, tramps through the mud of the works on days of twelve to eighteen hours, and climbs into the cab of a steam shovel on the canal works. They stop in Puerto Rico on the way home.
tours.anchor: 1906-11-08 leaves Washington on the Mayflower; 1906-11-26 back in Washington

tours.title: Down the Mississippi
tours.short: Down the great river by steamboat, into the Louisiana canebrakes, and home to a panic.
tours.summary: Roosevelt dedicates the McKinley Memorial in Canton, then boards a stern-wheeler at Keokuk for what he called his first trip on the Mississippi, leading a fleet of steamers and speaking for a deeper waterway. He spends two weeks after bear in the canebrakes of northeastern Louisiana, first on Tensas Bayou and then at Bear Lake, and gets one near the end of the hunt. The Panic of 1907 breaks in New York while he is on his way back to Washington.
tours.anchor: 1907-09-29 leaves for a three-week tour; 1907-10-23 home to the Panic

tours.title: Smithsonian-Roosevelt African Expedition
tours.short: A year collecting for the Smithsonian across East Africa and down the Nile.
tours.summary: Days out of office, Roosevelt sails with Kermit for British East Africa. From Mombasa they ride the railroad into the game country and spend the year hunting and collecting specimens for the Smithsonian across what are now Kenya and Uganda, then travel through the Lado Enclave and down the Nile to Khartoum, where Edith and Ethel join him.
tours.anchor: 1909-03-23 sails on the Hamburg; 1910-03-14 Edith and Ethel join him at Khartoum

tours.title: From Khartoum to England
tours.short: From Khartoum to England, with some of his best-known speeches.
tours.summary: Reunited with Edith, Roosevelt travels from Sudan and Egypt through Italy, Austria-Hungary, France, the Low Countries, Scandinavia, Germany and Britain. He gives Citizenship in a Republic at the Sorbonne, delivers his Nobel lecture in Christiania, rides beside the Kaiser to watch German army manoeuvres, and speaks his mind on Egypt at London's Guildhall. He sails from Southampton, and New York gives him a hero's welcome home.
tours.anchor: 1910-03-15 with Edith and Ethel at Khartoum; 1910-06-18 welcomed home in New York

tours.title: Western Tour and the New Nationalism
tours.short: Nearly three weeks in the West, and the New Nationalism at Osawatomie.
tours.summary: Back from abroad and pulled into politics, Roosevelt heads west in a private car. In Osawatomie, Kansas, he delivers The New Nationalism, the speech that set out the program he would carry into 1912.
tours.anchor: 1910-08-23 tour begins; 1910-09-11 home

tours.title: Across the South and West, 1911
tours.short: Nearly six weeks across the South and the West; Edith and Ethel join him in the Southwest.
tours.summary: Roosevelt speaks his way from Atlanta through Texas to the Southwest, where Edith and Ethel join him at Albuquerque. In Arizona he rides down the Bright Angel Trail into the Grand Canyon with Archie and dedicates the dam on the Salt River that bears his name. At Berkeley he gives the Earl Lectures and, in his Charter Day address, makes his famous boast about taking the Canal Zone, then comes home through the Pacific Northwest and Montana.
tours.anchor: 1911-03-08 leaves for the South and West; 1911-04-16 home to Oyster Bay

tours.title: Coast to Coast for the Bull Moose
tours.short: A month crossing the country as the Progressive candidate for President.
tours.summary: From Connecticut to California and back through the South, Roosevelt takes the Bull Moose campaign to the whole country. He draws more than 20,000 at the Minnesota State Fair and, in San Francisco, answers Woodrow Wilson's argument that the history of liberty is a history of limiting government power.
tours.anchor: 1912-09-02 Connecticut kickoff; 1912-10-02 home to Sagamore Hill

tours.title: The Great Lakes Tour and Milwaukee
tours.short: The campaign tour that ended with a bullet in Milwaukee.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sets out on another campaign swing through the Midwest, by way of Chicago and Wisconsin. In Milwaukee, outside the Gilpatrick Hotel, he is shot in the chest by John Schrank. He gives his speech anyway, then spends nearly a week in Chicago's Mercy Hospital before going home to Sagamore Hill.
tours.anchor: 1912-10-07 leaves on a Great Lakes tour; 1912-10-14 shot in Milwaukee; 1912-10-22 home

tours.title: Grand Canyon, Rainbow Bridge and the Hopi Mesas
tours.short: Seven weeks in the canyon country with his sons Archie and Quentin.
tours.summary: Roosevelt crosses the Grand Canyon and climbs to the North Rim by the Bright Angel trail, hunts cougars along the rim with his sons and their cousin Nicholas, rides through the desert to Lees Ferry and Navajo country, camps beneath Rainbow Bridge, and watches the Hopi snake dance at Walpi.
tours.anchor: 1913-07-07 leaves with Archie and Quentin; 1913-08-26 home

tours.title: South America and the River of Doubt
tours.short: A lecture tour and museum collecting trip that became the descent of the River of Doubt.
tours.summary: Roosevelt sails for South America to lecture, then joins Brazilian explorer Cândido Rondon to trace an unmapped river through the Amazon basin. On the River of Doubt the party loses men and canoes, Roosevelt nearly dies of an infected leg and fever, and the river is renamed the Rio Roosevelt.
tours.anchor: 1913-10-04 sails on the Vandyck; 1914-05-19 homecoming

tours.title: Madrid and London for Kermit's Wedding
tours.short: Across the Atlantic for Kermit's wedding in Madrid.
tours.summary: Barely home from Brazil, Roosevelt sails for Spain with his daughter Alice. He sees Kermit marry Belle Willard in Madrid and goes on to London to speak to the Royal Geographical Society about the River of Doubt.

tours.title: West to the Expositions
tours.short: West by the Canadian Rockies to the expositions, preaching preparedness.
tours.summary: With war in Europe, Roosevelt crosses Canada to the Pacific and travels down to San Francisco for a Roosevelt Day at the Panama-Pacific International Exposition, then on to San Diego's exposition. National preparedness is the theme of his exposition speeches.
tours.anchor: 1915-07-11 off to California; 1915-08-02 back in New York

tours.title: The West Indies
tours.short: About six weeks in the Caribbean, and a statement from Trinidad.
tours.summary: Roosevelt and Edith sail for a rest in the Caribbean, calling at islands from St. Thomas to Martinique, spending about a week in British Guiana and ending in Trinidad. From Trinidad he issues a written statement that he will not fight for the Republican nomination. He and Edith sail home together on the Matura.
tours.anchor: 1916-02-11 sails; 1916-03-24 home from Trinidad

tours.title: Western Swing for Hughes
tours.short: A western swing campaigning for Charles Evans Hughes.
tours.summary: With reporters along on his special train, Roosevelt stumps for the Republican nominee from Kentucky to Arizona and New Mexico and back through Colorado and Chicago.
tours.anchor: 1916-10-17 western swing begins; 1916-10-28 Brooklyn

tours.title: Devilfishing in Florida
tours.short: Harpooning giant rays in the Gulf as the country goes to war.
tours.summary: Roosevelt travels by way of Punta Gorda to a floating camp off Captiva Island to hunt devilfish with Russell Coles, a Virginia amateur who was the leading expert at harpooning them. On the way home he stops in Washington on April 3, the day after President Wilson asks Congress to declare war.
tours.anchor: 1917-03-23 leaves for Florida; 1917-04-03 back in New York
